issues.legal_issue: A homicide committed during a sudden, unpremeditated fight in the heat of passion, without undue advantage or cruel conduct, falls within the sudden-fight exception to murder even if several injuries were inflicted and one proved fatal.
material_facts: A dispute over the return of a kitchen led to a heated argument and sudden quarrel, with no evidence of prior ill-will or premeditation.
During the argument, one participant took out a penknife; the appellant went into the adjoining kitchen, picked up a knife, and inflicted a simple injury on that participant.
The deceased intervened in the scuffle and suffered three knife injuries, one of which proved fatal.
The court found that the number of injuries did not, in the circumstances, establish cruel or unusual conduct or the taking of undue advantage.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was entitled to the benefit of Exception 4 to Section 300 of the Indian Penal Code. The murder conviction was set aside and replaced with a conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part I.
issues.legal_principle: Exception 4 to Section 300 of the Indian Penal Code applies when there is a sudden fight, no premeditation, action in the heat of passion, and no undue advantage or cruel or unusual conduct. The cause of the quarrel and who provoked or started the assault are immaterial; the number of wounds is not decisive. A person who, in a sudden quarrel and heat of the moment, uses a handy weapon and causes a fatal injury may receive the exception’s benefit if the other requirements are met. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: appeal_from_murder_conviction and sudden_fight and no_premeditation and heat_of_passion and absence_of_undue_advantage_and_cruel_conduct

predicates.appeal_from_murder_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for murder.
predicates.sudden_fight: The fatal violence occurred during a sudden fight arising from a quarrel.
predicates.no_premeditation: The assailant had not planned the violence before the quarrel.
predicates.heat_of_passion: The assailant acted in the heat of passion during the quarrel.
predicates.absence_of_undue_advantage_and_cruel_con: The assailant did not take undue advantage or act cruelly or unusually.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a murder conviction concerns a fatal act during a sudden fight, without premeditation, in the heat of passion, and without undue advantage or cruel conduct, the conviction is reduced to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
